rules.text: The JB74's factory tail pipe exits at the REAR RIGHT - the driver's side in a JDM RHD car - below the rear bumper, pointing rearward and very slightly down. It is a plain unfinished pipe of roughly 38-45 mm outer diameter with no decorative tip, and it does NOT protrude past the bumper face: it sits flush to about 10 mm behind it, so from directly behind the car you see a dark hole under the bumper rather than a tip. Centre height is about 330 mm above ground (estimated: measured off APIO's and Monster Sport's full-car rear photos against the tyre OD; consistent with FUJITSUBO publishing 320 mm as the minimum ground clearance at the front of its tail on the same car). EVIDENCE for the side: (a) Kakimoto's spec tables give 出口方向 S(右) for both the GTbox 06&S cat-back and the Class KR rear-piece-only, and a rear-piece-only bolts to the factory centre pipe so it cannot change sides; (b) Kakimoto's own fitted photo of the GTbox shows the tip on the flank where the steering wheel is visible through the door glass, and the car is RHD, so that flank is the car's right; (c) the fuel filler flap is on that same right-hand rear quarter; (d) Monster Sport states its Sp-X exit aligns with the stock bumper position and its photos put the tip on the same side.

For a configurator there are only FIVE distinct rear-end silhouettes, and geometry can be shared inside each: (1) REAR RIGHT SINGLE - stock position, one tip under the right of the bumper (HKS LEGAL K-1 and LEGAL K-1 Titan, Fujitsubo A-K, Kakimoto GTbox, Kakimoto Class KR rear piece, Monster Sport Sp-X/Sp-R, JAOS BATTLEZ, Showa Comfort, APIO Shizuka Gozen). (2) REAR TWIN LEFT+RIGHT - one tip under each bumper corner, symmetric (Kakimoto Class KR S71355S, GReddy Cross Exhaust). (3) SIDE EXIT LEFT, TWIN - two tips out of the left rocker just ahead of the rear wheel, rear bumper untouched (HKS LEGAMAX TrailMaster, Kakimoto Class KR DS edi.). (4) SIDE EXIT LEFT, SINGLE, at the bumper corner (Showa Garage Links / Links Blue Tail). (5) SIDE EXIT RIGHT, SINGLE, high bullet through a hole in the rear bumper (TANIGUCHI Compe Muffler R). APIO's Yoshimura systems are family 1 but with the silencer itself turned into the visual feature.

Japan no longer uses a JASMA sticker as the legal gate. Since the 2010 (Heisei 22) acceleration-noise rules, a replacement muffler must carry a pre-certification display - in practice a JQR number on a welded plate - and every system in this file that is sold for road use in Japan carries one: HKS LEGAL K-1 and K-1 Titan JQR10181175 (both codes share the number), HKS TrailMaster JQR20202008, Fujitsubo A-K JQR10181118, Kakimoto GTbox JQR30192030, Class KR L+R JQR20192028, Class KR rear piece JQR10191029, Class KR DS edi. JQR20252140, JAOS BATTLEZ ZS JQR20183167. FUJITSUBO additionally displays the JASMA mark. Certification is per-variant, so read the fine print: APIO's Shizuka Gozen is certified for JB64 all types and JB74 type 5, but NOT for JB74 types 1-4 (those need the centre-muffler version); TANIGUCHI's Compe R is a certified product yet measures 91 dB proximity on a JB74 against 81 dB stock, which is legal in Japan but loud; HKS's TrailMaster is not certified for the type-5 AT car. The Australian systems (GReddy is JDM but sold there, Manta, Redback) carry no JQR plate. For TAIWAN the relevant test is the local noise limit measured at the tailpipe, not a Japanese certificate: a Japanese JQR plate has no legal standing at a Taiwanese inspection, and a system measuring 88-92 dB proximity (HKS TrailMaster 88, Kakimoto GTbox 92, TANIGUCHI 91, GReddy 92 per side) is at or over what a Taiwanese annual inspection will pass on a 2018+ car. The quiet ones - HKS LEGAL at 83 dB (the quietest here, only 2 dB over the 81 dB stock reading), JAOS BATTLEZ at 83 dB, Fujitsubo A-K at 84 dB, Kakimoto Class KR rear piece at 84-85 dB, Showa Comfort at 86 dB - are the realistic Taiwan choices. Note the two HKS systems sit at opposite ends of this list: the LEGAL is the quietest product in the file and the TrailMaster is among the loudest. NOTHING here was verified against a published Taiwanese ruling; treat the Taiwan half of this rule as engineering judgement, not law.

Rear bumper and exhaust are NOT independent choices in this configurator. Documented interactions: FUJITSUBO A-K is 標準バンパー車専用, stock bumper only, and the OEM mud flaps must be removed or cut. JAOS BATTLEZ ZS (B702518B) needs a partial cut of the stock bumper and cannot coexist with the OEM mud flap set; JAOS sells a SEPARATE part number (B702513A) for cars wearing the JAOS rear sports cowl. APIO ships every Yoshimura and Shizuka Gozen system in two part numbers, one for the OEM bumper and one for APIO's own tactical bumper, because the pipe run differs. TANIGUCHI's Compe R needs a hole drilled through the stock rear bumper and is designed to fit TANIGUCHI's own rear bumpers without cutting - and the cover garnish that hides the hole is made for JB64 types 1-3 only, so on a JB74 with the stock bumper the cut edge stays raw. SHOWA GARAGE's Links is designed around Showa Garage's own bumper spoiler; on a stock bumper it needs a partial cut, it leaves only 10-15 mm clearance to the spoiler when correctly seated, and Showa explicitly says fitment to JB74 type 4-5 stock bumpers is unconfirmed. HKS's TrailMaster and Kakimoto's DS edi. sidestep the whole problem by exiting through the rocker, but the HKS kit needs the floor undercover modified on type 4 and later cars. HKS's LEGAL needs no bumper work at all, but it is the tightest fit to the stock bumper in this file: HKS's manual tells the fitter to check テールパイプとバンパの位置関係、クリアランス and warns the tail can touch and melt a plastic bumper under hard use, and a Taiwanese JB74 owner had the tip knocking the stock bumper on start-up shake until a longer hanger was fitted. Treat LEGAL plus any aftermarket rear bumper as UNVERIFIED for the same reason as the other rear-exit systems, and flag the stock-bumper clearance as marginal rather than clean. WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: no maker publishes compatibility with KLC, DAMD, URNIETA or ARB rear bumpers. Every one of those replaces the bumper's lower rear face, which is exactly where a rear-exit tip passes, so the configurator should treat any rear-exit system plus a non-OEM rear bumper as UNVERIFIED rather than silently allowing it. The two side-exit families are the only ones that are safe to combine with an arbitrary rear bumper.

No true quad-exit (four tips) system exists for the JB74 from any maker checked. The maximum is TWO tips, in three arrangements: one tip per side at the rear (Kakimoto Class KR S71355S, 96 mm slash; GReddy Cross Exhaust G-Style, 90 mm), both tips on the left rocker (HKS LEGAMAX TrailMaster, 75 x 2; Kakimoto Class KR DS edi., 70 x 2), or a single tip. BLITZ does build a NUR-SPEC Quad Model but its fitment list has no Jimny of either body. An earlier note calling the Showa Garage Links Blue Tail a dual system is wrong - see corrections.

The November 2025 facelift (type 5) breaks fitment in both directions and the configurator must carry the year. Both HKS lines - TrailMaster 32018-AS006 and LEGAL 31013-AS017/AS020 - fit types 1-5 but NOT the type-5 AT; the LEGAL's manual states the exclusion as 'JB74W 2025/11～ ＡＴ車適合外'. APIO's Shizuka Gozen uses different part numbers for JB74 type 5 (2004-03R/03P) than for the earlier car. JAOS BATTLEZ ZS explicitly does not fit 2025.11+ cars. Kakimoto certifies the same parts for both eras but publishes different noise figures (GTbox 92 dB on 2018-2025 cars, 89 dB on type 5). Fujitsubo's 750-81927 covers both eras with one number and also supersedes the discontinued 750-81901.

Weight is the quick tell for how much of the car changes. A REAR SECTION ONLY (axle-back) weighs 3.5-4.5 kg and replaces just the last silencer and tip: HKS LEGAL 4.0 kg (one piece, 分割数 1, bolts to the stock centre pipe's rear flange with a single 45 mm gasket and two rubber hangers), Fujitsubo A-K 3.7 kg (stock rear section 4.4 kg), Kakimoto Class KR rear piece 4.1 kg (stock 4.5 kg), Monster Sport Sp-X/Sp-R 3.6 kg. A CAT-BACK weighs 8-11 kg and changes the whole visible under-run from the catalyst back: Kakimoto GTbox 8.8 kg (stock 8.7), Class KR L+R 10.2 kg, DS edi. 9.5 kg, HKS TrailMaster 9.0 kg, JAOS BATTLEZ 10.3 kg, APIO Shizuka Gozen with centre pipe about 10 kg (stock 8.5). The APIO/Yoshimura titanium system is the outlier at 4.2 kg for a full system against roughly 8 kg stock. For a 3D model this matters because an axle-back only needs new geometry behind the rear axle, while a cat-back changes what is visible along the whole right-hand underbody in a low side view.

HKS sells THREE part numbers for the JB74W, across TWO product lines, and they point in opposite directions. (1) LEGAL K-1, code 31013-AS017, ¥49,500 - a single-piece rear section, polished SUS304, one 74.7 mm straight-cut tail, exiting REAR RIGHT under the bumper in the stock position. HKS's own product page calls it 右側シングル出しレイアウト. (2) LEGAL K-1 (Titan), code 31013-AS020, ¥71,500 - the same part with a titanium/burnt-blue tail. (3) LEGAMAX TRAILMASTER, code 32018-AS006, ¥150,700 - a cat-back with twin 75 mm tips out of the LEFT rocker, invisible from behind. If an owner says their HKS exits on the same side as the factory pipe and points rearward under the bumper, it is a LEGAL, not a TrailMaster; the TrailMaster cannot be confused with stock because it deletes the rear exit entirely. The two LEGAL codes each cover JB64W, JB74W and JC74W on ONE part number, which is why a JB64 listing for 31013-AS017 is not evidence against JB74 fitment. METHOD: every HKS muffler series - current (Cool Style II, Hi-Power 409, Hi-Power Spec-L II, LEGAL, LEGAMAX, LEGAMAX Premium, LEGAMAX Sports, Silent Hi-Power, Spec-R, SSM, Super Turbo Muffler, Superior Spec-R, LEGAMAX TRAILMASTER, Vii-TS) and discontinued (2SX, 3SX, Cool Style, Cool Style Square, ES Premium, ES Wagon, ES Wagon 409, Full Dual, Hi-Power, Hi-Power Spec-L, Touring Spec-L) - was fetched as its full fitment table from hks-power.co.jp/product_search/product/1/type/<id>/stock and .../status/9 and grepped for JB74W. Only type 11 (LEGAL) and type 105 (TRAILMASTER) return a JB74W row. Cool Style II, LEGAMAX Premium, LEGAMAX Sports, Silent Hi-Power and Hi-Power Spec-L II all return zero. Super Turbo Muffler (type 17) has a JB64W row (SSR, 90 mm, 31029-AS004, ¥106,700) but NO JB74W row. The HKS front-pipe, centre-pipe and metal-catalyst fitment tables were also checked and contain no JB74W. Do not confuse 32018-AS006 with 31021-AS004: that is the JB64 TrailMaster, ¥149,600, centre pipe sized for the R06A turbo. HKS is also the co-development partner behind TANIGUCHI's Compe Muffler R and Nomad Compe N, which is why those two look and sound like HKS products without carrying the HKS name.

Taiwan has almost no real JB74 exhaust market. What is actually on sale locally (Ruten, verified 2026-09) is cosmetic slip-over tip covers at TWD 618-1,610 from a dozen resellers - these change the visible tip without changing a single pipe, which is worth its own configurator entry because it is what most Taiwanese JB74s actually wear. Beyond that, MyRack lists the JAOS BATTLEZ ZS at about TWD 22,000 (plain) / TWD 24,000 (titanium-colour tail) and a Taiwanese retailer has listed the APIO x Yoshimura stainless Cyclone at about TWD 72,500. THE ONE REAL EXCEPTION IS HKS'S LEGAL MUFFLER, and an earlier version of this rule got it wrong. 31013-AS017 is stocked in Taiwan as 公司貨 (official import) at TWD 13,800 by 童夢國際 / DOME Racing Taiwan on Ruten and Yahoo auctions and by 汽車零件王 on Shopee, and the titanium-tail 31013-AS020 is listed at TWD 16,900 by PP Performance; HKS Taiwan's own LINE account (@hkstw) has promoted the LEGAL for the Jimny as 現貨供應中. That makes the HKS LEGAL the CHEAPEST proper branded exhaust available in Taiwan for this car - cheaper than the JAOS - and the New Jimny JB74 Taiwan Club has owner install reports of it going back to 2021. The TrailMaster, by contrast, has no published TWD price; hks.com.tw returns an almost empty page and carries no Jimny catalogue, so it remains a special order. Everything else - Kakimoto, Fujitsubo, Showa Garage, TANIGUCHI, Monster Sport - reaches Taiwan only by personal import. Expect roughly 1.4-1.7x the Japanese list price landed, on the same pattern the wheel atlas records.

Both twin side-exit systems put hot pipework immediately below the left rocker, ahead of the rear wheel, where a side step or rock slider would normally go. HKS fits a branded perforated heat shield over that run and Kakimoto ships a 17-piece bracket kit (STF.KIT66) to hang it. In the configurator, a side-exit exhaust and a left-hand side step/slider should be treated as a probable clash - no maker publishes compatibility either way.

muffler.visibleNote: This is the single most silhouette-changing exhaust for the car. In a pure side view of the LEFT flank you see a bright perforated cylindrical silencer running under the rocker and two burnt-blue tips at its rear end. From directly behind, the car looks completely stock.

tw.note: HKS Taiwan (昶和企業, hks.com.tw) is the official agent but publishes no Jimny catalogue or price. Special order only.

systems.groundClearanceNote: HKS 装着時地上高 数値 210mm, キット対象部位 フロントリーディングアーム. Read this as the lowest road clearance on the car with the kit on, measured at the front leading arm - not as the height of the silencer or the tips.
systems.notTheOwnersSystem: If a JB74 owner reports an HKS exhaust that exits on the stock (right) side and points rearward under the bumper, it is NOT this product. The TrailMaster removes the rear exit completely - see hks_legal_k1.
systems.modelling: Model this as a LEFT-FLANK feature, not a rear feature - it is the only system here that is invisible from behind. Under the left rocker, from roughly the B-pillar back to just ahead of the rear wheel, lay a horizontal polished cylinder about 100 mm in diameter and 450 mm long, wrapped in a perforated heat shield with a visible bead-rolled band and a small HKS-logo plate. Out of its rear face run two round 75 mm tubes side by side, turned a few degrees outboard, ending in slash-cut mouths with heavy blue-to-gold heat gradation on the last 40-60 mm - the classic burnt-titanium look, darkest blue right at the rim with a rolled lip. Tip centres roughly 300 mm above ground, 20-40 mm proud of the rocker face, finishing 150-250 mm ahead of the rear tyre. The rear bumper and the stock right-hand exhaust hole are both removed from view: the stock tip geometry must be deleted when this system is fitted, and nothing replaces it under the bumper. A viewer looking at the rear three-quarter from the right will see an empty bumper underside and wonder where the exhaust went - that is correct.
systems.sideEvidence: HKS's own headline is シエラ専用設計のサイド出しデュアルマフラー (side-exit dual designed for the Sierra). The fitted photo on the product page is a flank shot with the car's NOSE POINTING LEFT, which is the car's left side, and the twin tips and the perforated shield are on that flank. Re-checked in this pass.

On the JB64 HKS warns the mud flap must be trimmed; on the JB74 an owner install note reports the flap clears as-is.

tip.finish: polished SUS304 (主要材質 S304), mirror bright over the whole system
tip.cut: straight, square-cut mouth with a thin rolled rim - not a slash
tip.arrangement: single, pointing rearward and turned a few degrees outboard, the tail pipe kicking up over the axle to reach the bumper
tip.sleeveLengthNote: ESTIMATED. Measured off HKS's own studio photo using the published 74.7 mm tip OD as the ruler: the tip sleeve reads about 1.07 tip diameters long.

position.exit: below the rear bumper, rearward, in the stock position - the factory hole is reused, nothing is cut
position.protrusionNote: ESTIMATED, 40-55 mm. Three lines of evidence, all pointing at 'clearly proud but tight': (a) CRAFT's before/after pair shot from the same low rear-quarter angle shows the stock pipe effectively flush under the bumper and the HKS tip standing roughly half to two thirds of its own 74.7 mm diameter clear of the bumper face; (b) HKS's own manual carries a caution that under hard driving テール部とバンパが干渉する場合があります and tells the fitter to check テールパイプとバンパの位置関係、クリアランス, which only makes sense for a tip finishing close to the bumper skin; (c) a Taiwanese JB74 owner (New Jimny JB74 Taiwan Club, 2021-09-17) reported 會頂到原廠後保桿 - the tip knocking the stock rear bumper on start-up shake - and cured it with a longer hanger, so on some cars the tip is touching the bumper rather than clearing it.
position.heightNote: ESTIMATED, 310-335 mm. HKS publishes no tip height. Pixel-scaled off HKS's own straight-on rear photo using the published 74.7 mm tip OD as the ruler gives about 300 mm, but that demo car wears oversized mud-terrain tyres which lift the body, so the figure on stock 195/80R15 lands a little lower in the frame and a little higher in millimetres. Cross-check: the tip sits immediately under the rear bumper's lower edge in the same photo, and the stock tip and the Fujitsubo tip both sit near 330 mm, so this system is in the same band.

muffler.visibleNote: At 4.0 kg the silencer is a compact round barrel that tucks up behind and above the rear axle; in a pure side view the rear wheel covers it and what you actually see is the bright tail pipe and the tip under the bumper. An owner fitting a hitch member reported タイコが小さいので全く干渉はありませんでした - the can is small enough to clear a tow hitch, which a bigger aftermarket can (Rosso Modello DUSSEL Ti-C) did not.
muffler.sizeNote: ESTIMATED, plus or minus about 20 percent. Scaled from HKS's studio photo against the published 50.8 mm mid-pipe diameter, giving roughly 150 mm across by 250 mm long - a stubby barrel about 1.5 diameters long. Cross-checked against mass: a 150 x 250 mm SUS304 shell with end caps, internals and about 900 mm of 50.8 mm pipe computes to 4.2-4.4 kg against HKS's published 4.0 kg, so the shape is right even if the exact numbers are not published.

The installation manual separately gives the post-fit vehicle minimum clearance as 約200 mm ホイールベース間 and 約200 mm トレッド間.
systems.kitContents: メインマフラー x1, ガスケット φ45 x1, ラバーステー x2, 取説/保証書/ステッカー. Fitting torque 29-34 Nm. One 14 mm spanner is the minimum tool list.
systems.modelling: This is the HKS that looks like a factory upgrade rather than a conversion, and it is the one a Taiwanese owner is most likely to have. Keep everything about the stock rear end and change only what hangs under the RIGHT of the bumper: delete the dull flush factory stub and put a mirror-polished 74.7 mm round tube in its place, mouth cut square (not slashed) with a thin rolled rim, standing about 45 mm past the bumper face with its centre near 325 mm above ground and turned a few degrees outboard. The tail pipe behind it rises steeply over the rear axle, so in a low rear three-quarter view you see a bright diagonal of pipe climbing away from the tip - that diagonal is the second read after the tip itself. The silencer is a small polished barrel roughly 150 x 250 mm hidden above and ahead of the axle; do not draw a fat can in side view. Rear bumper untouched, OEM mud flaps stay on, and from the left of the car nothing at all has changed.
systems.sideEvidence: Four independent lines, and they agree. (1) HKS's own product page text: 右側シングル出しレイアウト. (2) A Japanese installing shop repeats it unprompted: 右側シングル出しのシンプルなデザイン (craft-web.co.jp). (3) Photographic - HKS's fitted rear photos for both 31013-AS017 and 31013-AS020 are straight-on rear views and put the tip on the RIGHT of frame; in a rear view the car's right side IS the viewer's right, and the same test applied to FUJITSUBO's rear-quarter photo (where the near flank shows the steering wheel through the door glass, proving it is the right side of an RHD car) puts the A-K tip on the same side. (4) Structural, and decisive on its own: this is a ONE-PIECE rear section that bolts to the stock centre pipe's rear flange with a single 45 mm gasket. It has no crossover and cannot move the exit to the other side of the car, so it must exit wherever the factory pipe exits - which this file's stock-exit rule establishes as the rear right.

gaps: No maker publishes tip PROTRUSION past the rear bumper or tip HEIGHT above ground. Every protrusionMM and most heightMM values in this file are photo-scaled estimates, flagged individually. The only published height-class figures are FUJITSUBO 320 mm (minimum ground clearance at the front of the tail) and GReddy 268/278 mm (logo plate / rear silencer body). HKS's 装着時地上高 numbers - 210 mm for the TrailMaster, 270 mm for the LEGAL - are NOT tip heights and must not be used as such: HKS names the measurement point as a chassis part (front leading arm, stock second catalyst), so they describe the car's tightest road clearance with the kit fitted.

Silencer body dimensions are almost never published. Only two hard numbers exist: Kakimoto's タイコ径 115 mm for the GTbox and APIO's 1,030 mm overall muffler length for the Shizuka Gozen. Everything else is estimated from photos.

The exact lateral offset of the HKS and Kakimoto side-exit tips from the rocker face could not be measured - both are estimated at 20-40 mm from side photos. If the configurator needs to check clearance against a side step, this number must be measured on a real car.

5ZIGEN's own exhaust search lists ジムニーシエラ and ジムニーシエラ(ショートバンパー用) as selectable vehicles, but the results page is JavaScript-only and no part number, price or spec could be retrieved. 5ZIGEN is confirmed as the co-development partner on all three SHOWA GARAGE systems; whether they also sell an own-brand JB74 muffler is UNRESOLVED.

BLITZ: the muffler line index and the NUR-SPEC StyleD fitment page were checked and contain no Jimny of either body. BLITZ's 2026 new-product feed for JB74W lists only a suction kit and lift-up dampers. No BLITZ JB74 exhaust was found, but BLITZ's partsnavi search is form-driven and could not be queried directly, so this is a strong negative rather than a proven one.

Sense Brand could not be located at all - sense-brand.jp, sense-brand.com and sense-brand.co.jp all fail DNS. Either the domain is different or the company no longer trades. No Sense Brand JB74 exhaust was found.

TANIGUCHI does not publish a product code for the Compe Muffler R, and the 'Exceed' muffler recorded in the earlier accessory atlas does not appear anywhere in TANIGUCHI's current catalogue - see corrections.
No maker publishes compatibility between any exhaust and the KLC, DAMD, URNIETA or ARB rear bumpers. This is the single biggest unknown for a configurator that lets both be fitted.
Kakimoto's 出口方向 letter codes (S / W) are undocumented. The parenthetical side - 右 / 左 / 左右 - was used instead and cross-checked against their fitted photos; the letter itself is ignored here.

Taiwanese pricing now exists for three brands: HKS LEGAL (TWD 13,800 plain / TWD 16,900 titanium tail, official import), JAOS (MyRack) and one APIO listing. No Taiwanese price could be found for the HKS TrailMaster, Kakimoto, Fujitsubo, Monster Sport, Showa Garage or TANIGUCHI, and hks.com.tw still publishes no Jimny catalogue - the Taiwanese HKS LEGAL trade runs through resellers and HKS Taiwan's LINE account rather than the website.

Nobody publishes the HKS LEGAL's silencer dimensions or its tip protrusion, and the two are the weakest numbers in that entry. The silencer is scaled from a studio photo against the published 50.8 mm pipe and cross-checked against the published 4.0 kg mass, so it is right to about plus or minus 20 percent. The protrusion is bracketed rather than measured: a Taiwanese owner reports the tip actually TOUCHING the stock rear bumper until a longer hanger was fitted, while HKS's own photos show it standing clearly proud - so real cars vary, and a configurator should treat 40-55 mm as a range, not a value. Both want a tape measure on a real car.
Noise figures are maker-measured proximity readings under the Japanese method. No independent measurement, and nothing measured under a Taiwanese test procedure, was found for any system.
corrections: HKS DOES make a rear-exit, stock-side muffler for the JB74, and this file previously denied it. THE OLD CLAIM (rule hks-which-system, and the HKS corrections entry below it, compiled 2026-09-21): 'There is exactly ONE HKS muffler in the HKS catalogue for the JB74W: LEGAMAX TRAILMASTER, code 32018-AS006' and 'HKS's other muffler lines (Super Turbo, Hi-Power Spec-L II, LEGAMAX Sports, LEGAMAX Premium, SSM, Cool Style II, Hi-Power Spec-R, Superior Spec-R, Silent Hi-Power, Hi-Power 409, LEGAMAX, LEGAL) have no JB74 entry', with that single TrailMaster entry described as a LEFT-side twin exit through the rocker that leaves the rear bumper untouched. WHAT THE EVIDENCE NOW SAYS: HKS's LEGAL line does have a JB74W entry - two codes, in fact. 31013-AS017 (polished SUS304, JPY 49,500) and 31013-AS020 (titanium-colour tail, JPY 71,500) are both a single 74.7 mm tail exiting REAR RIGHT under the bumper in the stock position, both JQR10181175, both 4.0 kg one-piece rear sections, both 83 dB proximity against 81 dB stock. HKS's own product page for 31013-AS017 says 右側シングル出しレイアウト in as many words; the LEGAL fitment table (product_search product/1/type/11/stock) lists ジムニーシエラ 3BA-JB74W K15B 18/07- against both codes; the installation manual is headed 3BA-JB64W・3BA-JB74W・3BA-JC74W; and HKS's fitted photos for both codes are straight-on rear views with the tip on the right of frame. The TrailMaster description was itself accurate - it really is a left-side twin - but it was never the only HKS option, and it is the WRONG answer for an owner whose HKS exits like stock. The error came from checking HKS's other lines by browsing product pages instead of fetching each series' fitment table; this pass fetched all 25 HKS muffler series tables, current and discontinued, and grepped every one for JB74W.

HKS's 210 mm is not the TrailMaster's ride height. The old entry read 'HKS publishes 210 mm as the lowest point of the whole kit'. HKS's 装着時地上高 block gives 数値 210mm with キット対象部位 フロントリーディングアーム - the front leading arm, a chassis part - so the figure is the tightest road clearance anywhere under the car with the kit fitted, not the height of the silencer or the tips. The LEGAL's equivalent entry is 270 mm at the 純正第2触媒 with the explicit remark 製品装着による最低地上高変化はありません, which settles the reading: these numbers describe the car, not the exhaust.

The HKS LEGAL is sold in Taiwan with a published TWD price, so the old taiwan-market claim that HKS's Taiwan agent 'carries no Jimny catalogue at all, so a TrailMaster is a special order with no published TWD price' is only half right. It stays true of the TrailMaster. It is false of the LEGAL: 31013-AS017 is stocked as 公司貨 at TWD 13,800 by 童夢國際 / DOME Racing Taiwan on Ruten and Yahoo auctions and by 汽車零件王 on Shopee (both describe it as 尾段 尾出, rear section / rear exit), the titanium-tail 31013-AS020 is listed at TWD 16,900 by PP Performance, HKS Taiwan's LINE account has promoted it as 現貨供應中, and the New Jimny JB74 Taiwan Club carries owner install reports going back to 2021-09-17. At TWD 13,800 it undercuts the JAOS BATTLEZ ZS and is the cheapest branded exhaust on sale for this car in Taiwan.

HKS's Super Turbo Muffler is a JB64-only product, not a JB74 one. Its fitment table (type 17) carries ジムニー 3BA-JB64W R06A(TURBO), shape SSR, 90 mm tail, 31029-AS004, JPY 106,700, and no JB74W row at all. Cool Style II, LEGAMAX Premium, LEGAMAX Sports, Silent Hi-Power, Hi-Power Spec-L II, Hi-Power 409, LEGAMAX, SSM, Spec-R, Superior Spec-R, Vii-TS and every discontinued HKS muffler series were checked the same way and return zero JB74W rows; so do HKS's front-pipe, centre-pipe and metal-catalyst tables. The complete HKS exhaust catalogue for this car is therefore three part numbers: 31013-AS017, 31013-AS020 and 32018-AS006.

SHOWA GARAGE Links Blue Titanium P00211 is NOT a dual-exit system. The earlier accessory atlas recorded it as 'DUAL side exit' with two 70 mm tips; Showa's own product text describes a single テールエンド 70φ ダウン形状 and the product photo shows one tip. It is a single left exit with a blue-coated rolled-lip tip. Corrected here.

TANIGUCHI 'Exceed' does not exist in TANIGUCHI's catalogue. A full sweep of ors-taniguchi.co.jp returns only the Compe Muffler R (JB64/JB74 types 1-4), the Nomad Compe N (JC74), the Competition Muffler 3 Quiet (JB23-43) and accessories. The 'Exceed' entry in the earlier atlas came from a third-party price roundup and could not be substantiated.

The earlier atlas's 'HKS Regal / Regal Ti at about JPY 30,515' was closer to the truth than the correction that replaced it, and both were wrong. 'Regal' is a misreading of LEGAL (リーガル), which IS a real HKS line and DOES have a JB74 part - 31013-AS017 at JPY 49,500, with a titanium-tail sibling 31013-AS020 at JPY 71,500, which is exactly the 'Regal / Regal Ti' pair the old atlas half-remembered. Its price was wrong (JPY 30,515 is below even the discounted street price) and nothing about it was verified, but the product existed. The 2026-09-21 correction then over-corrected, declaring the LEGAMAX TRAILMASTER 32018-AS006 'the one and only HKS muffler for the JB74W'. Both entries are superseded: HKS has three JB74 codes, the LEGAL pair exits rear right like stock, and the TrailMaster exits out the left rocker. (The old atlas's 'rear centre' description was wrong for all of them - the JB74 has no centre exit.)

Almost every 'rear centre' exit recorded in the earlier accessory atlas is wrong. The JB74 has no centre exit. Stock and the great majority of aftermarket systems exit REAR RIGHT; a minority exit rear left+right, left-side or right-side. Entries previously marked 'rear centre' for JAOS, FUJITSUBO, APIO, Monster Sport, Kakimoto, 5ZIGEN and HKS have been re-sided in this file from maker spec tables and fitted photographs.

Kakimoto's JB74 range is four products, not one. The earlier atlas recorded only an unverified 'Class KR' at a street price of JPY 44,921. The real line-up is GTbox 06&S S44355 at JPY 115,500, Class KR left+right S71355S at JPY 170,500, Class KR rear piece S71355R at JPY 69,300 and Class KR DS edi. side exit S71355WS at JPY 121,000.

Monster Sport Sp-X and Sp-R are NOT separate JB64 and JB74 parts. One part number each - 241590-5600M and 241590-5500M - covers both bodies. The tail end on both is 76.3 mm, not unpublished as previously recorded.

JAOS BATTLEZ ZS requires a partial rear bumper cut. The earlier atlas recorded it as a straightforward one-hour fit with no bumper work; JAOS's own page says 一部バンパーカットが必要 and that it cannot be used with the OEM mud flap set.
FUJITSUBO 750-81901 is discontinued and superseded by 750-81927. The A-K tail is φ70 with a 21-degree slash - the earlier atlas recorded the dimension as 'NOT PUBLISHED'.

method.searchBudget: The session's web-search quota was exhausted before this research began, so no search engine was usable. Everything here came from direct fetches of maker sites plus reading the product photographs themselves. The 2026-09-22 HKS revision worked the same way, with one addition: r.jina.ai was used as a plain-text read proxy in front of DuckDuckGo's HTML endpoint, which restored a usable result list without spending search quota. That is what surfaced the Taiwanese retail listings and the owner reports.
method.hksSweepMethod: HKS's catalogue is enumerable and should be enumerated rather than browsed. /product/exhaust/index.html lists every current muffler series and /product/discontinued lists every retired one; each series page contains exactly one link of the form /product_search/product/1/type/<id>/stock, and that page is the complete plain-HTML fitment table for the series (add /status/9 for the discontinued variant of the same table). Fetching all 25 tables and grepping for JB74W is about 30 seconds of work and is the only way to be sure a line has no entry. This is how the LEGAL was found after an earlier pass had declared it absent.
method.sideDetermination: Left and right were established photographically, not assumed. A flank photograph of a JDM RHD car shows the steering wheel on the near side only when the camera is on the car's right; Kakimoto's GTbox fitted photo shows exactly that, together with the fuel filler flap on the same quarter, and the tip on that same flank - which matches Kakimoto's own 出口方向 S(右). The same test applied to Kakimoto's DS edi. and HKS's demo car places both of those side-exit systems on the car's LEFT.
method.dimensionEstimates: Where a dimension is marked ESTIMATED it was scaled from a product photograph using the fitted tyre's outer diameter as the ruler, and the reasoning is written into the field's own Note. No dimension in this file was invented.
